Jean-Luc Brunel Jeffrey Epstein — EFTA01972778, the MC2 account email.

December 5, 2012: the MC2 modeling agency's office sends an account statement — to close an account — to Richard Kahn, Jeffrey Epstein's personal accountant. Kahn resolves a withheld-check discrepancy in writing ("you will be getting back 4,380 of the 5,000 mistakenly withheld from your check"), with Brunel and Epstein both copied. Epstein's financial office sat inside MC2's payment plumbing.

A second document, in Brunel's own words (EFTA00962798, June 2013): he asks Jeffrey's permission to repaint the apartment Epstein provided him — "I have never asked anything have always been very thankful for what Jeffrey is doing." Epstein forwards it to staff with one word: "follow up."

What these documents establish is business entanglement and patronage. What they do not mention is conduct — that record lives in court filings and allegations, and this archive keeps the two separate.

Alan Dershowitz Jeffrey Epstein — EFTA00352969, Epstein's own itinerary.

Thursday, February 12, 2015: Lesley Groff writes to Epstein, "Working on your itinerary for today... Rich Joslin and Alan Dershowitz both needed to meet you earlier... Alan is confirmed..." The schedule for the day Epstein flew in from St. Thomas ends: "4:00pm Appt w/Alan Dershowitz." Eight months later, October 14, 2015, the office schedule again lists "5:00pm Appt w/Dershowitz" (EFTA00338082).

The full record, carried both ways: Dershowitz was on Epstein's defense team for the 2007–08 Florida case — a documented professional relationship. The allegation that made him famous in this story was withdrawn: in November 2022 Virginia Giuffre dropped her lawsuit against him, saying she may have made a mistake identifying him. He has always denied any wrongdoing.

A schedule is a plan, not proof a meeting occurred — the archive publishes it as a plan. What it documents is scheduled access in 2015, in Epstein's own office paper.

Bill Richardson Jeffrey Epstein — EFTA00014374, the prosecutors' own memo.

August 18, 2019: an SDNY prosecutor writes up a call with Bill Richardson's counsel about the allegation unsealed days earlier in the Giuffre civil papers. The memo's read of that deposition: Richardson "was ordered to, but doesn't appear to say that anything actually happened." And: prosecutors did not intend to subpoena him or request an interview — "there are not specific allegations that we need to hear his side of at this time."

The releases do document a phone channel — in January 2017 Epstein's scheduler relayed that Richardson would call Epstein in ten minutes (EFTA02662212). Contact is documented. The allegation itself remained an allegation: Richardson denied it, he was never charged, and he died in 2023.
